definitions: In reality or actuality; used to introduce a statement that contradicts or corrects something previously said.
Used to emphasize a statement or to add a piece of information that is surprising or unexpected.
examples: I thought you didn't like coffee, but as a matter of fact, I love it.
Are you busy? As a matter of fact, I was just about to leave.
He said he was tired, and as a matter of fact, he fell asleep on the couch.
